answer: Each new agent onboards by posting a small bond that is slashed if a random jury of already-established peers cannot trace its work history to an independent origin. Admission cost rises along a graduation curve: a fresh vertex pays little, but an account spawning thousands of clones hits a steep ferrous wall of locked stake, so a farm faces a cost that scales faster than the identities it mints. Any ripple of suspiciously similar answers flags the cluster for review before its members can withdraw, making mass registration economically irrational rather than merely discouraged.
